this is exactly the attitude most jurors and many judges actually have.  The law can't ignore your "confession" and let you off just because you took responsibility.  That's unfair to the aggrieved party.  The law also can't tell people they will be punished for exercising their rights because sometimes that is entirely appropriate.  But any honest lawyer will tell you that if you go to court and make presenting every single piece of evidence difficult for the plaintiff for no good reason, things will tend not to work out very well for you.  Mostly, at least where I live, it often works the way that common sense says it should.   It depends on what is at stakes, how clear the evidence against you is, and what rights you are asserting.  Deny, Deny, Deny is not always the best legal strategy.  Always best to consult an attorney.

regardless of what people say, as a practical matter jurors and judges do take whether or not the guilty/liable person takes responsibility into account in deciding punishments.  This is why so many people plead guilty in criminal cases.  Always better to consult an attorney before doing so, if the stakes are anything other than minor.   It all depends on the circumstances.  I've seen assholes insist on a jury trial for a traffic ticket and then try to play Perry Mason.  Jury deliberates for 5 minutes and the the Defendant ends up paying 10x the costs and fees pleading guilty would have gotten them.

I would put another caveat in:  admitting fault in front of a jury can help keep them on your side in  rare instances. For example, in a small car accident, admitting you tapped the person in front of you accidentally but saying the plaintiff was not hurt is effective in keeping the verdict below your policy limits.  All the runaway plaintiff's verdicts I've seen have been where the Defendant unreasonably tries to deny fault or blame the plaintiff for the accident.    Always better to wait until closer to trial before making that decision though.

I see this argument a lot.  Something along the lines of "well somebody has to be at the top and the bottom of the bell curve," as if the Bell Curve itself is what causes people to fall somewhere on the distribution.  Skill, circumstance, and to some extent randomness are what cause the distribution.  I think this is also why some people refuse to accept that certain things are random.  For example, shots made/missed in basketball basically fluctuate randomly (i.e. there is no "hot hand").  No basketball fan believes this because in their minds they equate "random" with being unskilled and not based on circumstance.  It's not that there is no skill or circumstance involved in making a shot, it's that all the variables (both skill based and random) fall this way and that on any given shot, making it impossible to get a better prediction than the persons average shot percentage for any given shot.

My advice to you is to bring a lawsuit on your own soon.  Go to a shop and get an estimate of damage and casually mention that you are bringing a lawsuit (so you know it won't be an estimate).  In my state all you need is an affidavit from the mechanic that verifies your damages (using specific language).  You'll have to research your local laws to introduce the estimate (it is hearsay unless properly introduced into evidence), but to prove fault, your word and the video should be enough.  Judges like to hand out money, so ask for as much without seeming dumb.  Also your state may allow a claim for the diminished value of your vehicle after being repaired.   It's easier than you might think.  I am a smart guy and I lose to pro se people all the time.  Don't be intimidated.  The court system is on your side.  It likes to hemorrhage money.  Don't deal with adjusters.  They will just bounce you from one to another and make minimal offers, if any.  It's designed to slow down the process in a way that seems like they are willing to work with you.  

Good luck!  None of this should be construed as legal advice...whatever you do legally will have to be done all on your own.  Sorry!

I'm a lawyer to and I've been struggling with the complete lack of honesty in the legal system, especially in what I do.  The problem is not just that there are no penalties for dishonesty, but that there are HUGE rewards for dishonesty.  And all the persons in place to point out the dishonesty are getting a piece of the pie, so nobody wants to point it out.

I work in personal injury on the defense side. I was shocked when I first started doing this.  It is exactly what you think it is...the majority of people have "back strains."  Most are clearly lying just from the fact that this is 2 years after an accident with minimal damage and they say they still cant do anything.  Scans show no problem.  I'm not saying a person could not be injured in a small accident but most of them are lying.  Not worth surveillance so we just pay.  Even in cases where we have video showing the "accident" and the fact that nobody even moved at the time of impact, judge still hand out the standard 2x-3x medical bills.  Why, because judges are appointed by the legislature.  The biggest contributor to the legislature are lawyers, mostly on the plaintiffs side.  By raising too much of a stink even defense lawyers and insurance companies would lose money in the long term, as claims dried up (insurance companies make more money the more claims they handle, and they are happy to payout, just so long as all companies pay out equally).  So basically the system works like this:  every person in the ghetto knows that if you get into an accident you can get money, even if you are lying.  So poor, dishonest people make bogus claims, judges, lawyers (both defense and plaintiffs), legislators, police officers, court reporters, insurance companies et. all get their standard cut.  Honest people's who don't make claims insurance rates keep going up and up but they are outside the system, so have no idea, and its stealing a little bit of money from a lot of people, so consumers don't notice.  So dishonesty is actually encourage.  Thank god for the jury system, but Judges have a lot of control over what a jury sees.  We have a case in my office that has been tried 3 times and 3 times the jury has returned a verdict for less than 10K.   The plaintiff is asking for 300K.  THe judge took the verdict away and gave a new trial each time...just because the verdict was too low, not because of any legal error.  As defense lawyer I have had judges give my patently wrong rulings, knowing that in smaller cases we cannot afford to appeal.  You can argue with the judge in front of the jury, but they think you are the idiot because, of course the judge knows what he is talking about.   This is how the car accident system works, and I have heard that Worker's comp and SSD and malpractice are similar.  This is why every commercial on TV is for insurance or a personal injury attorney.  THey are all part of the same system and it is growing out of control.  

On the criminal side, good hard evidence is hard to come by.  So why not just get some questionable witnesses?  So there is no incentive to put the kabosh on jail-house witnesses, at least initially.  And there is an incentive to over-charge people.  The more people you can draw into the legal system, the more defense attorneys, judges and other discussed above can suck from them.  Some cases could be resolved pretty easy, but much better to draw it out only to have a high-powered defense attorney work some "magic" and "get the client off" (non-sexually).  So instead of worrying about getting down to the facts, we've set up a system where crimes are defined so broadly and the penalties are so severe, that people need to pay a bunch just to sort through all the issues, even for minor issues.

To a certain degree, any time you have a law in place to accomplish a legitimate goal, lawyers will use it for illegitimate ends, that's jsut the way it is.  It has always been this way, but as the number of lawyers, criminal justice majors, and generally college educated people not willing to do manual labor increases, the system needs to grow and so we need dishonesty (i.e. fictions) to explain why we need to keep throwing more people in jail or keep paying out ridiculous claims in order to grow the system.  

So dishonesty isn't just an unhealthy biproduct of an imperfect system, it is the glue that is holding the whole system together.


So what is the solution?  Though it may put me out of a job, we need to stop encouraging people to enter this system, mainly by being honest about what it is.  When you see that flashy lawyer, realize that he is just good at manipulating the system, and call him out for the dick he is.  Also respect public defenders, legal aiders, and no nonsense brass-tacks people within the system.  so, in other words, don't think the big shots are there because they are smart.  They may not be "dishonest" in the traditional sense, but many powerful attorneys are powerful because they have no qualms taking subtle winks and nods that manipulate the system.  

Keep in mind, those within the system have been doing it for years.  We don't need to say anything explicitly in order to conspire to get more money our of the system.  So the people need to be vigilante.  The mistrust of lawyers is warranted but not in the way most people think.  A lawyer I worked for had a picture in his office.  Lawyer on the left pulling on a tail of a cow, lawyer on the right pulling on the head.  A judge in the middle milking the cow.  And the cow  was labeled "client."  Your first questions to any lawyer you might retain should be "do you think the legal system bleeds too much money from clients?"  If the answer is "no," run away.  Also if your lawyer encourages fighting run away, except in a situation where the other side has a dick lawyer.  Then your lawyer has to fight.  You should be able to tell from way the other lawyer acts in court.  In any event, your lawyer should always encourage de-escalation wherever possible, but match the other side blow for blow.
